title: Map syllables to letters
observableEvidence: Maps a supplied pronunciation to a plausible letter sequence.
prompt: An invented word is said MAY-lest: two syllables, with the stress on the first. Its first vowel sounds like the name of the letter A, and its second syllable rhymes with "best". Choose the spelling that records these sounds.
solutionRepresentation: maylest. The letter pair ay spells the long a sound (the name of the letter A), and lest records the second syllable. In mellest, the e followed by a double l is read as the short e in "bell", and in mylest, the y is read with an i sound (as in "my" or "myth"); neither gives the long a sound.
solutionMethod: Match the described first vowel sound to the letters that usually spell it.

deterministicValidator.canonicalAnswer: Spelling that matches the sounds: maylest
acceptedAnswers: Spelling that matches the sounds: maylest
